summary: Iter 23 — Server-side pagination, sort and debounced search on row-level reports verified end-to-end. Backend pytest (test_reports_pagination.py): 16/16 PASS covering deal-blotter/settlement/audit-trail page+limit, page2 returns different rows, server-side sort_by=amount asc/desc, CSV+PDF still return full dataset (no pagination), settlement from_bank filter, audit-trail user_name filter, trader 403 on audit-trail, and aggregation reports (open-positions, volume-summary, client-activity, user-activity) confirmed to NOT return page/pages fields. Frontend Playwright on preview URL: pagination controls (First/Prev/Next/Last) render, Next loads new rows + sends page=2, sorting by Amount column resets to page=1 and sends sort_by=amount, 400ms debounce on Client filter (0 API calls during typing, exactly 1 call after 600ms), CSV/PDF buttons present, Settlement shows From/To Bank filters, Audit Trail (admin) shows User filter + pagination. Footer correctly shows '1-50 of 120 records / Page 1 of 3'. Found and fixed 1 critical regression: report_open_positions did not unpack new (rows, total) tuple from _get_deals_for_report -> 500 AttributeError. Old test_reports.py has 2 obsolete assertions (total==len(rows)) broken by intentional pagination change — not a defect, needs main agent to refresh those legacy assertions.

minor.issue: Legacy assertions in /app/backend/tests/test_reports.py::TestJsonFormat (test_deal_blotter_json, test_audit_trail_json_admin) check total==len(rows). With new default page=1/limit=50 pagination this is no longer valid (e.g., total=120 vs 50 rows). Update these two assertions to len(rows) <= limit and len(rows) <= total.

action_items: Refresh /app/backend/tests/test_reports.py::TestJsonFormat assertions to account for default pagination (total >= len(rows), len(rows) <= limit) instead of total == len(rows).
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED IN THIS RUN — server.py L1142 report_open_positions used `deals = await _get_deals_for_report(query, user)` while the helper now returns a (rows, total) tuple, producing a 500 AttributeError on every JSON/CSV/PDF call to /api/reports/open-positions. Patched to `deals, _ = await _get_deals_for_report(query, user)`. Recommend adding a unit test asserting open-positions returns 200 (now in test_reports_pagination.py).

_get_deals_for_report is the only helper, but the signature changed silently to return a tuple. Returning a tuple unconditionally is a foot-gun (open-positions regression proves it). Consider always returning a NamedTuple or a small dataclass `ReportPage(rows, total)` so call sites read `result.rows` and stay correct even when total is unused.

Aggregation endpoints (volume-summary, client-activity, user-activity, open-positions) still pull up to 50,000 deals/logs into memory with `.to_list(50000)` then aggregate in Python. As volume grows this will OOM the worker. These aggregations should move to MongoDB `$group` pipelines.

ReportsPage.jsx PAGINATED_REPORTS is hard-coded at the frontend (line 237). If a new row-level report is added on backend with pagination, two places must be edited. Better: have the backend echo `paginated: true` in the JSON response and let the FE branch on that flag.
Default limit on backend is 50 (cap 500); FE never sends `limit`, so users always see 50/page with no UI to change page size. Consider exposing a 'rows per page' dropdown for power users.

Sort header on FE only sends sort_by/sort_dir; backend whitelists no fields and passes the raw string into Mongo .sort(). A malicious user could sort by an unindexed huge field and hit slow queries. Add a server-side allowlist of sortable columns per report.

useDebounce custom hook re-creates a setTimeout on every keystroke (correct) but if the same value is re-typed (Test→Tes→Test) it still triggers a fresh fetch because debouncedValue ref-changes. Acceptable for now, but worth a memo guard if perf matters.

rca of the issue: open-positions 500: refactor of _get_deals_for_report changed return type from List[dict] to Tuple[List[dict], Optional[int]]. Three of four callers were updated; line 1142 in report_open_positions was missed. When code iterated the tuple, the loop var `d` became the list itself, hitting AttributeError on d.get(). Fix: unpack as `deals, _ = await _get_deals_for_report(...)`. Verified by adding test_open_positions_snapshot which now PASSes.
